name: Ashes to Ashes
editorial_article: "Ashes to Ashes," released in August 1980 as the lead single from David Bowie's album *Scary Monsters (And Super Creeps)*, stands as a pivotal moment in the artist's career, effectively closing the book on the 1970s and his earlier glam and Berlin-era experimentations. Produced by Bowie alongside long-time collaborator Tony Visconti, the track is perhaps most famous for its subversion of the folk-hero narrative established in Bowie’s 1969 breakthrough hit, "Space Oddity." By revisiting the character of Major Tom eleven years later, Bowie transforms the once-optimistic pioneer into a disillusioned, drug-addicted figure decaying in the void of space. \n\nMusically, "Ashes to Ashes" is characterized by a haunting, nursery-rhyme-inspired melody—Bowie acknowledged the influence of the 1950s song "The Inch Worm"—layered over an innovative three-bar loop and shimmering synthesizer textures. This sonic aesthetic, coupled with its unflinchingly dark lyrics, solidified the track's status as a masterpiece of late-era new wave and art-pop. The lyrics, most notably the bridge "I never done good things / I never done bad things / I never did nothing out of the blue," provide a chilling, soul-baring moment that suggests both profound regret and existential detachment. The track remains a cultural touchstone for its groundbreaking music video and its willingness to confront the disillusionment of the modern era, marking a definitive shift toward the experimental sounds that would define Bowie’s artistic transition into the new decade.

editorial_teaser: A haunting, art-pop reimagining of the Major Tom saga, "Ashes to Ashes" serves as both a melancholic nursery rhyme for the 1980s and a powerful, disillusioned farewell to Bowie's own past.
